Vinkivtsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jewish presence in Vin'kivtsi dates to the 16th century, surviving Crimean Tatar raids and Cossack uprisings under both Maksym Kryvonis in 1648 and the later Koliivshchyna rebellion. The community grew to a majority of the town's population twice — 56 percent by 1897 and 52 percent again by 1939 — before Nazi occupation from July 1941 led to two mass executions in 1942 that killed over 2,300 people. The cemetery today is split between a severely overgrown, mostly demolished old section and a well-maintained new part that has continued to receive at least one recent burial, alongside several mass graves located just outside its gates.
